problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-3x(t)-2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[-1,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options below regarding the given system.$\,$
$y=\frac{1}{2}x$ is {{field-1}} line.

$\,$
{{field-2}} is {{field-3}} line.

$\,$
The equilibrium point (origin) is {{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ is $\text{a stable}$ line.

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=-x$ is $\text{a stable}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\text{a stable node (sink)}.$ 

**Note:** The phase portrait of the system looks as follows:
